name: Question 1
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/5907cf8a9103cc9a639fd8078da3646cc0395d28827f58c0f1beef0a1c06645b.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y,\,\,0\le z\le {y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a89646433c8851f66c94092b75fae7b46b01f31c69ca03d338464b87bd7f5df4.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
y=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/1604e44050208cfb3b4dd81d35bff9769c7498d8304583d5ba92ad4b2f62fd05.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

Question 1

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0y∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then y, and then x.

a
 ∫01∫x2x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
b
 ∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
c
 ∫01∫0x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
d
 ∫01∫0x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
e
 ∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤y≤1,0≤x≤y,0≤z≤y2−x2}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,0≤x≤y}

To change the order of integration from dzdxdy to dzdydx, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is

x=y⟹y=x

and the top boundary of the region is

y=1.

Then, the type I representation of the region D is

D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,x≤y≤1},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx.
